scope: local offline reserve-adapter stdin interface with supplied report fixtures; no fresh genesis or preparer invocation

checks: Actual child processes execute prepare and review against synthetic externally selected reports; output equals the existing pure adapter and preserves all disabled permission flags.
Exact u64 reserve balance digits survive the JSON transport without conversion to a floating-point amount.
Missing, extra or unsupported command arguments, malformed or empty input and wrong external selectors refuse with no report or supplied private marker in diagnostics.
The reader accepts split chunks and refuses empty, oversized, failed and stalled input streams; the deadline test uses a bounded shortened fixture timeout.
Oversized buffers and invalid UTF-8 refuse before JSON selection; invalid reader bounds are rejected.
Output and diagnostic pipe failures retain refusal status without exposing underlying errors.

limitations: This exposes the existing pure adapter to a bounded subprocess transport. It does not connect reserve replacement to the genesis preparer.
Inputs and reports are supplied fixtures. Their hashes select bytes but do not independently establish execution, custody, backing or history.
The 30-second deadline bounds input collection. Callers must independently bound the entire process, drain stdout/stderr and discard stdout on any nonzero exit, including output-pipe failure.
Runtime/dependency artifact admission, external planning selectors, fresh compilation, output comparison and two strict slot-zero replays remain integration requirements.
No compiler, key generator, replay, validator, RPC or deployment was invoked by the adapter tests.
